top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 100, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Ford RideLondon's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
When someone attacks on flat to gently rolling closed paved roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Ford RideLondon. Practice on flat to gently rolling closed paved roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 100 miles.
Ford RideLondon's flat to gently rolling closed paved roads rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Ford RideLondon. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,900ft of climbing on flat to gently rolling closed paved roads does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on flat to gently rolling closed paved roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
At Ford RideLondon, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
100 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 100 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Ford RideLondon. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Ford RideLondon’s 100 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 100 miles of flat to gently rolling closed paved roads in London / Essex, England.
